WiFi = Wireless LAN
PPP = Point-to-point communication
ATM = High-speed cell switching
ARP = IP → MAC mapping
SDLC = IBM protocol
HDLC = Advanced SDLC version

12/05/2026, 09:55 - Waqar AkhtarUsar: Ethernet
 Most common wired LAN technology
 Works at Data Link Layer
 Uses MAC addresses
 Devices connected using cables + switches
 Uses CSMA/CD for collision handling
 Fast + reliable for offices/labs

Example: College computer lab LAN

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

 WiFi (IEEE 802.11)
 Wireless networking technology
 No physical cable needed
 Uses radio waves
 Works at Data Link Layer
 Uses CSMA/CA instead of CSMA/CD
 Provides mobility

Example: Home WiFi router

PPP (Point-to-Point Protocol)
Used for direct communication between 2 devices
Common in WAN links
Supports authentication
Error detection supported
Works over serial links

Example: Old ISP dial-up connections
12/05/2026, 09:57 - Waqar AkhtarUsar: ATM (Asynchronous Transfer Mode)
 High-speed networking technology
 Transfers fixed-size cells (53 bytes)
 Used in telecom + backbone networks
 Supports voice, video, and data
 Very fast but expensive

Example: Telephone company backbone networks

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

ARP (Address Resolution Protocol)
Converts IP address → MAC address
Works between Layer 2 and Layer 3
Needed inside LAN communication

Example:
PC knows IP = 192.168.1.5
Uses ARP to find MAC address

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

 SDLC (Synchronous Data Link Control)
 Developed by IBM
 Data Link Layer protocol
 Used in WAN communication
 Supports error + flow control
 Basis for HDLC

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

HDLC (High-Level Data Link Control)
 Improved version of SDLC
 Bit-oriented protocol
 Used in WAN links and router communication
 Provides framing + error detection
 Cisco routers commonly use HDLC by default on serial links

12/05/2026, 10:24 - Ojus MathurUsar: Nyquist Theorem (No noise)
Maximum data rate:
C = 2B log₂ M
Where:
C = capacity
B = bandwidth
M = signal levels
Shannon Theorem (Noisy channel)
C = B log₂ (1 + S/N)
Where:
S = signal power
N = noise power
Important: Shows maximum possible speed.

12/05/2026, 14:46 - Akshat Talwar USAR: ARQ (Automatic Repeat reQuest) is a reliable data transmission protocol used in networks.
Its main purpose: ensure data sent over an unreliable channel reaches correctly.
Works on the principle of error detection and retransmission.
Uses ACK (Acknowledgment) and NACK (Negative Acknowledgment) messages to confirm receipt.
2. How ARQ Works
Sender transmits a frame (packet) to the receiver.
Receiver checks the frame for errors (usually via CRC or checksum).
If correct, receiver sends ACK → sender sends next frame.
If incorrect or lost, receiver sends NACK → sender retransmits the frame.
12/05/2026, 14:49 - Akshat Talwar USAR: CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check) is an error-detecting code used in digital networks and storage devices.
It detects accidental changes in raw data during transmission or storage.
Based on polynomial division of the data.
Widely used because it can detect single-bit, double-bit, burst errors efficiently.

17/05/2026, 22:15 - Geetansh USAR Vats: #include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

void djkstraa(int n , int cost[10][10] , int s , int dist[10]){
    int visited[10];
    int count = 1,min,v;
    // initialize
    for(int i = 1 ; i <= n ; i++){
        visited[i] = 0;
        dist[i] = cost[s][i];
    }
    visited[s] = 1;
    dist[s] = 0;

    while(count<n){
        min = 9999;
        // find min dist
        for(int i = 1 ; i <= n ; i++){
            if(dist[i]<min && visited[i]==0){
                min = dist[i];
                v = i;
            }
        }
        visited[v] = 1;
        // update distances
        for(int i = 1 ; i <= n ; i++){
            if(visited[i]==0 && dist[v] + cost[v][i] < dist[i]){
                dist[i] = dist[v] + cost[v][i];
            }
        }
        count++;
    }
}

int main(){
    int i,j,n,s,cost[10][10],dist[10];
    printf("enter number of nodes : ");
    scanf("%d",&n);
    printf("enter cost matrx\n");
    for(int i = 1 ; i <= n ; i++){
        for(int j = 1 ; j <= n ; j++){
            scanf("%d",&cost[i][j]);
            if(cost[i][j]==0){
                cost[i][j] = 9999;
            }
        }
    }
    printf("\n enter source vertex \n");
    scanf("%d",&s);
    djkstraa(n,cost,s,dist);
    printf("\n shortes path from %d is \n",s);

    for(int i = 1 ; i <= n ; i++){
        if(s!=i){

#include <stdlib.h>

void bell(int n , int cost[10][10] , int s , int dist[10]){
    //initialize
    for(int i = 1 ; i <= n ; i++){
        dist[i] = 9999;
    }
    dist[s] = 0;
    // relax v-1 edges
    for(int k = 1 ; k <= n-1 ; k++){
        for(int i = 1 ; i <= n ; i++){
            for(int j = 1 ; j <= n ; j++){
                if(cost[i][j]!=9999 && dist[i]+cost[i][j]<dist[j]){
                    dist[j] = dist[i]+cost[i][j];
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

int main(){
    int i,j,n,s,cost[10][10],dist[10];
    printf("enter number of nodes : ");
    scanf("%d",&n);
    printf("enter cost matrx\n");
    for(int i = 1 ; i <= n ; i++){
        for(int j = 1 ; j <= n ; j++){
            scanf("%d",&cost[i][j]);
            if(cost[i][j]==0){
                cost[i][j] = 9999;
            }
        }
    }
    printf("\n enter source vertex \n");
    scanf("%d",&s);
    bell(n,cost,s,dist);
    printf("\n shortes path from %d is \n",s);

    for(int i = 1 ; i <= n ; i++){
        if(s!=i){
            printf("%d -> %d = %d ",s,i,dist[i]);
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

17/05/2026, 23:39 - Waqar AkhtarUsar: Suppose you are playing a game where each bet has a 40% chance of winning and a 60% chance of losing. You start with 2,000 chips, and your goal is to place bets totaling at least 10,000 chips. If you reach a cumulative bet amount of 10,000 chips, you immediately win; if you ever lose all your chips before that point, you lose.

For instance, if you bet 20 chips, those 20 chips count toward the 10,000-chip target regardless of whether you win or lose that particular bet. After placing this bet, your chip count will either increase to 2,020 (if you win) or decrease to 1,980 (if you lose).

Your minimum bet size is 1 chip, and your maximum bet size is whatever you currently have.

Given these conditions, what betting strategy maximizes your probability of reaching the goal and winning the game? What do you estimate is your probability of winning under this strategy?

17/05/2026, 23:40 - Akshat Talwar USAR: @⁨Meta AI⁩ answer
17/05/2026, 23:40 - Meta AI: Woah, MST and algorithms ka heavy dose! 😅 Let's break it down:

1. *Imp Viva questions for MST*:
    - What's Minimum Spanning Tree?
    - Applications of MST?
    - How do Prim and Kruskal algorithms work?
2. *Bellman vs Dijkstra*:
Bellman-Ford handles negative weights, Dijkstra doesn't. Use Bellman for graphs with negative weights.
3. *Priority queue real-life use*:
Managing tasks with varying priorities, like hospital ER triage or job scheduling.
4. *Prim vs Kruskal*:
Prim's: Grows tree from a node, efficient for dense graphs.
Kruskal's: Selects edges, simpler to implement.
Use Prim for dense graphs, Kruskal for sparse.
5. *Strassen's multiplication*:
Divides matrices into sub-matrices, reduces multiplications. Recurrence: T(n) = 7T(n/2) + O(n^2).
6. *Time complexities*:
    - Prim's: O(E + V log V)
    - Kruskal's: O(E log E)
    - Dijkstra's: O(E + V log V)
    - Bellman-Ford: O(VE)
    - Strassen's: O(n^log2(7))
7. *Greedy vs DP*:
Greedy: Faster, optimal solution if problem has greedy choice property.
DP: More versatile, solves overlapping subproblems.
Greedy not better when optimal solution isn't guaranteed (e.g., 0/1 Knapsack).

Want specific examples or deeper dive into any? 😊
17/05/2026, 23:40 - Akshat Talwar USAR: @⁨Meta AI⁩ specific answers elaborate each
17/05/2026, 23:40 - Meta AI: Let's break it down 🔍:

## 1. Imp Viva questions for MST
- *What's Minimum Spanning Tree?*: A subgraph connecting all vertices with minimum total edge weight, no cycles.
- *Applications of MST?*: Network design (LAN, telecom), circuit design, transportation networks.
- *How do Prim and Kruskal algorithms work?*:
    - Prim's: Grows tree from a node, adds min-weight edges.
    - Kruskal's: Selects min-weight edges, avoids cycles.

## 2. Bellman vs Dijkstra
Bellman-Ford handles negative weights, detects negative cycles. Dijkstra's is faster but fails with negative weights.

## 3. Priority queue real-life use
- Hospital ER triage: Patients treated based on urgency.
- Job scheduling: Prioritizing tasks in OS or servers.

## 4. Prim vs Kruskal
- *Prim's*: Dense graphs, starts from a node.
- *Kruskal's*: Sparse graphs, sorts edges.

## 5. Strassen's multiplication
Divides matrices into sub-matrices, reduces multiplications from O(n³) to O(n^2.81). Recurrence: T(n) = 7T(n/2) + O(n²).

## 6. Time complexities
- Prim's: O(E + V log V)
- Kruskal's: O(E log E)
- Dijkstra's: O(E + V log V)
- Bellman-Ford: O(VE)
- Strassen's: O(n^2.81)

## 7. Greedy vs DP
- *Greedy*: Fast, works for problems with greedy choice property (e.g., Huffman coding).
- *DP*: Solves overlapping subproblems (e.g., 0/1 Knapsack).

Need more examples or clarity on any? 😊

    - DP: Breaks problem, solves it smartly.

18/05/2026, 01:00 - Geetansh USAR Vats: #include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <stdlib.h>

int main(){
    char text[] = "ABCDEFAB";
    char pattern[] = "AB";
    int n = strlen(text);
    int m = strlen(pattern);
    int found = 0;
    // btute force approach
    for(int i = 0 ; i <= n-m ; i++){
        int j;
        for(j = 0 ; j < m ; j++){
            if(text[i+j]!=pattern[j]){
                break;
            }
        }
        // pattern found
        if(j==m){
            printf("pattern found at index %d \n",i);
            found = 1;
        }
    }
    if(found==0){
        printf("no pattern found");
    }
    return 0;
}

31/05/2026, 15:24 - Ojus MathurUsar: pseudocode 

FractionalKnapsack(W, items)

Sort items by (profit/weight) in descending order

profit = 0

for each item

    if item.weight <= W
        profit += item.profit
        W -= item.weight

    else
        profit += item.profit * (W/item.weight)
        break

return profit

31/05/2026, 20:15 - Arghyadeep USAR: function spanningTree(V, edges):
    1. Build adjacency list from edges: adj[u] = (v, weight)
    2. Initialize:
       - visited = array of size V filled with False
       - pq = Min-Heap storing (weight, node)
       - total_cost = 0

    3. pq.push((0, 0))  // Start at node 0 with 0 weight

    4. while pq is not empty:
         weight, node = pq.pop()

         if visited[node]: continue
         visited[node] = True
         total_cost += weight

         for neighbor, edge_weight in adj[node]:
             if not visited[neighbor]:
                 pq.push((edge_weight, neighbor))

    5. return total_cost








 MST-PRIM(V, edges)
1   for each u ∈ V
2        do visited[u] ← False
3   cost ← 0
4   Q ← ∅                              // Min-priority queue storing (weight, vertex) pairs
5   INSERT(Q, (0, 0))                  // Start at vertex 0 with a weight of 0
6   while Q ≠ ∅
7        do (weight, u) ← EXTRACT-MIN(Q)
8           if visited[u] == False
9               then visited[u] ← True
10                   cost ← cost + weight
11                   for each (v, w) ∈ Adj[u]   // v is the neighbor, w is the edge weight
12                        do if visited[v] == False
13                             then INSERT(Q, (w, v))
14  return cost

10/06/2026, 02:01 - Dhairya Narula USAR: abe claude ne boht sahi smjha dia mujhe ye
10/06/2026, 02:01 - Dhairya Narula USAR: CSMA — Carrier Sense Multiple Access
"Listen before you talk"
Before transmitting, a station checks if the channel is idle. Three variants based on what happens when channel is busy:
VariantBehavior when busy1-persistentKeep listening; transmit immediately when idle (greedy, more collisions)Non-persistentWait a random time, then check again (less collision, more idle time)p-persistentWhen idle, transmit with probability p (balance between above two)
Problem: CSMA still can't detect collisions during transmission.

CSMA/CD — Collision Detection
Used in wired Ethernet (802.3)

Station listens while transmitting
If it detects a collision → immediately stops + sends a jam signal
Then waits using Binary Exponential Backoff before retrying
After kth collision → random wait from {0, 1, ..., 2^k - 1} slots
Works well for wired; not usable in wireless (can't hear own collision easily)


CSMA/CA — Collision Avoidance
Used in wireless networks (WiFi / 802.11)

Can't detect collisions reliably → avoid them instead
Uses IFS (InterFrame Space) + random backoff timer
Optionally uses RTS/CTS (Request to Send / Clear to Send) handshake to reserve channel
ACK required for every frame to confirm delivery
